content: {"summary":"CAT‑E301 spikes happen when the cache does not deliver. A lost Redis VM shows ETIMEDOUT (no response), while a Redis process that is still starting returns LOADING. In the 26 Oct 2025 incident the error was LOADING, indicating a restart; in the 9 Dec 2025 incident the error was ETIMEDOUT, indicating the VM was gone. In both cases catalog‑db‑01 absorbed the extra reads and its CPU rose to about 90% before returning to normal.","likely_cause":"Cache unavailability – either a vanished Redis VM (ETIMEDOUT) or a Redis process still loading (LOADING) – caused the CAT‑E301 spike; catalog‑db took on the extra load, spiking to ~90% CPU.","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"On 26 Oct 2025 the cache returned LOADING, showing the Redis process was still starting, not a lost VM.","evidence_ids":["INC-0094#0"],"quote":"Each failed cache lookup from catalog-api-02 came back from redis-cache-02.prod.internal with one word: `LOADING`."},{"text":"ETIMEDOUT indicates the Redis VM is gone or unreachable, while connection refused means the host is up but Redis isn’t listening.","evidence_ids":["RB-017#1"],"quote":"`ETIMEDOUT` means the Redis VM is gone or unreachable (a dead host sends no reset)."},{"text":"On 9 Dec 2025 the redis‑cache‑01 VM was gone, causing ETIMEDOUT errors.","evidence_ids":["INC-0108#0"],"quote":"The redis-cache-01 VM is gone."},{"text":"During both incidents catalog‑db‑01 CPU spiked to about 90% as reads shifted from cache to the database.","evidence_ids":["INC-0108#0"],"quote":"catalog-db-01 CPU reached about 90%."},{"text":"After failover the cache is empty, so catalog‑db load stays high until hot keys are repopulated.","evidence_ids":["RB-017#5"],"quote":"catalog-db CPU is back to its usual range."}],"next_checks":["Check the Redis error returned to catalog‑api (ETIMEDOUT vs LOADING vs connection refused).","Ping the redis‑cache VM or query Sentinel for primary status to confirm host reachability.","Monitor catalog‑db‑01 CPU and CAT‑E301 rate side‑by‑side during the outage.","Verify that Sentinel quorum is healthy if failover does not occur.","Observe cache warm‑up progress and watch database load decrease."]}
